concerns.quote: The chest Xray taken on the 13th January 2019 showed an image which was at least at the upper end of normal and in the context of a differential diagnosis of aortic dissection should have led to a CT Aorta being undertaken. Plain X rays are not diagnostic of aortic dissections. The consultant radiographer who reviewed the X ray remotely on the 14th January 2019 reported it as normal but had not been made aware of the differential diagnosis of aortic dissection. concerns.hazard: failure to order CT Aorta for suspected aortic dissection

concerns.quote: It is common practice for reviews of X rays to be undertaken by radiographers. The clinical information provided to them is sparse. More detailed and specific information would assist them in undertaking their reviews.

categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

promises.quote: The guidance was reviewed on 18" May 2021 by Clinical and Operational leads in NELFT and Barts Health. It has now been submitted to the joint governance and operational group for consideration and sign off at the next session on gh June 2021.
promises.summary: Reviewed streaming guidance and submit to governance for sign-off

promises.quote: The Royal College of Emergency Medicine is in the process of finalising a Guideline, based on the limited evidence that is available on the selection of patients for CT scanning. This will be circulated to our 10,000+ members and published on our website for public viewing. It is planned that this will be endorsed by the Royal College of Radiologists, to raise awareness amongst Radiologists.
promises.summary: Develop and publish a guideline on CT scanning for aortic dissection

concerns.quote: far too many doctors are missing the diagnosis of thoracic aortic dissection
concerns.hazard: missed diagnosis of thoracic aortic dissection

concerns.quote: misdiagnosis of acute aortic dissection is a systemic issue in the NHS which currently leads to many unnecessary deaths
concerns.hazard: systemic misdiagnosis of acute aortic dissection

concerns.quote: in half of patients presenting with acute aortic dissection, the diagnosis is not considered and about a third of patients are actively treated for the wrong diagnosis
concerns.hazard: delayed or incorrect treatment of acute aortic dissection

concerns.quote: around 500 patients each year die from acute type A aortic dissection, due to a delayed diagnosis or failure to make the diagnosis
concerns.hazard: preventable deaths from acute type A aortic dissection

concerns.quote: the feature of central chest pain that radiates to the throat and jaw stands out as important and deserving attention in guidance to raise the profile of acute aortic dissection. Emergency physicians know that chest pain radiating to the neck and jaw may indicate acute coronary syndrome, but rarely appreciate this also raises the prospect of acute aortic pain.
